plan: A kirtan lit as call and response: the room goes out wherever the track goes out — five real holes the producer left — and every time it comes back it comes back changed, from the leader's saffron through the congregation's rose to white at the two turns that matter, the D-minor-to-D-major hinge at bar 15 and the peak at bar 44.

states.why: The show opens with NO state before bar 1, so the first 1.8s are true black and the lead voice brings the light with it. Bars 1-3 are 25-37% loud with 1-5 hits: two lamps, low and warm, is the whole idea.

Bar 4 is the first real drum activity (7 hits, percussion and congas) so the bed starts moving here. every_beats 2 because the song is still at 89bpm and pulse at 1 lifts the rig ~5x a beat, which reads as a fault.
Bars 7-8 are tuba, wind, brass and trombone holding tones with 1 drum hit each — a plain held fill, which is what wash is for. Moving it to the outer pair hands the room across from the left pair.
Measured at 21.5-25.0s: violin, viola, timpani and congas swell in and lead-vocal takes the top lane at 23.0. The whole rig, and the colour turns back to saffron for the voice.

Bars 12-14 carry 0-1 drum hits and fall to 26% loud — the coldest, emptiest stretch of the first half. Indigo and nearly out. On the left pair rather than the inner one: par_8 and par_15 were the over-correlated pair at 0.754, and the quiet states are where that gets decided.

The hinge. Harmony turns D:min to D at 33.80s, drum hits jump 0 to 12 in a bar, guitar/strings/acoustic-guitar all enter. A hard hit on every beat from a very low floor is literally what the drums just started doing, and it comes straight out of a blackout.
Bars 19-21 are 63/61/68% loud, the loudest of the first half, driving straight at the chorus — but travelling, not hitting, so the drive bed stays unspent until the chorus actually arrives at bar 22.

The chorus arrives and the climax at 52.76s sits inside this span. Rose leads the pair now — the congregation's section. Colours swapped against the bar 18-22 drive so the arrival is a change, not a continuation.
Bar 30 measures 48% loud against neighbours at 74-82%, loudness 0.153 against 0.316. One bar where the room comes down but every beat still lands — a 33-second section has to breathe somewhere.

back-vocal enters at 66.0s and the call-and-response runs to bar 38 (lead vs back correlate -0.75 here). Rose for the responders. every_beats 2 because this is a 14-second span and a 5-lift-per-beat bed across it would flicker.

The section's second breather, bar 38 at 50% loud. Same bed as bar 30 deliberately — these are the same musical event twice, so they get the same word with a different colour, which is a palette rather than a repeat.

The loudest stretch of the song opens here at 86% and holds 79-89%. Starting at bar 39 rather than the section edge leaves 0.49s of black at 81.27-81.76 where loudness reads 0.137 — the hole the arrival lands out of.
Bars 44-45 at 88/85%. This and the next state are the show's brightest plateau, built to sit under the loudest 5-second window of the recording, which centres at 97.0s — not at the 92.5s headline.

Bars 46-47 are the two loudest bars in the song (90%, 92%). The colour turns from marigold to rose exactly on the section seam at 96.26s, so the brightest eight seconds of the show still changes in the middle instead of sitting there.
Piano, keys and digital-piano take the top lanes at bars 48-49 and loudness drops from 0.42 to 0.32 — the section thins here even though it is still loud. The left pair travels with it.

The other half of the same six seconds: par_15 and par_22 hold still while par_1 and par_8 travel. Two disjoint extents across one span is how a four-lamp rig gets two layers, and it is the only way the right pair ever stops moving in lockstep.
Woodwind, harmonica and flute at bar 51 then back-vocal and kick at 52 — the chorus gathers itself for the last two bars before the outro empties the room.

Covers from the section edge so 108.76-109.76 stays lit while the track is still at 0.365, then carries the collapse. The bed changes to breakdown exactly where the outro starts and the strip gesture pulls it down.

There is deliberately NO state across bars 54-55 (111.74-113.75) — that is the void, left to the isolate and the blackout. The room comes back here as bass, acoustic-guitar and then harp and banjo return at 32-44% loud.
Bar 57 rises to 54% with strings, double-bass and acoustic-guitar, and drum onsets climb 5 to 8 to 9 per two seconds. Indigo because the harmony is still D:7 and D:min until 120.0s.

The last vocal phrase. At 124.0-125.5 bowed_strings, cello, acoustic-guitar and dobro all touch 1.00 and the voice reaches 0.91 — the fullest the outro gets. The harmony is D major, so the room is simply warm and still and lets the swell do the moving.

Measured: the last vocal tail decays 127.0 (0.24) to 128.0 (0.04) and every one of the 39 lanes reads 0.00 from 128.5s. Two lamps at an ember follow the voice down, then nothing covers the last 2.8s and the room is genuinely out.

bindings.why: french-horn measures mean 0.400 and 66% of the intro above 0.3 — it is the melodic voice of the invocation, and it is the one lane here that is neither the drums nor the singer. One lamp given to it for 25 seconds, floor 0 so it goes out between phrases rather than hovering.

strings measure median 0.722 across this section — it is the lane actually carrying it. On the outer pair only, so the inner pair keeps the drone/pulse/drive beds and the room has two layers instead of one. response 2.2 makes the lamp drop out between phrases rather than hover.

9-13 drum onsets a bar — tambourine, congas, kick, snare. This is the kirtan groove and it should land on the struck hits, not the grid. Inner pair only so the drive bed still carries brightness on the outer; rest 0.03 so the inner pair is genuinely dark between hits instead of sitting at a floor.

Measured across this section: back-vocal means 0.59 while lead-vocal has dropped to 0.10 — the congregation is carrying it alone, so one lamp should be theirs. extent single is par_15 only, and floor 0.36 keeps it bright enough not to dent the peak plateau the other three lamps are holding.

kick is a top-three lane in five of this section's eight bars. One lamp punches with the bass drum while the other three hold the plateau — a spiky source against a smooth bed is the only thing that makes a lamp genuinely disagree, and floor 0.56 measured: at 0.50 this lamp pulled the show-brightest window off the song-loudest one, at 0.56 it sits back on it.

dobro means 0.387 with 65% of the outro above 0.3 — the slide is what carries this section, and it is named at bar 60. floor 0 and response 2.4 matter here: the outer pair has to reach near-zero across the void at 111-113s or the darkness does not happen.

gestures.why: Loudness 0.112 here and 0.060 on the next beat — the track falls away to almost nothing (moment 4). One blackout renders about half a second, so this is the first of a stacked pair.
The second of the pair. Together they hold a real hole of about a second across 32.7-33.75s, which is what makes the hinge land.

THE HINGE. Harmony turns D:min to D major at 33.80s, drum hits go 0 to 12 in one bar, guitar/strings/acoustic-guitar all enter at once. Out of a second of black, white on every lamp. Nothing else is anchored to this downbeat so nothing can cancel it.

The build into the chorus, bars 19-21 climbing 63 to 68% with 11-12 hits a bar. A gesture rather than a state so it lifts the strings binding on the outer pair as well as the bed on the inner — the whole room arrives together. `to` is held at 0.58 on purpose: measured at 0.92 this build became the brightest passage in the entire show at 181 DMX, brighter than the peak, and a build that outshines the peak is a show out of step with its own song.
The producer's own blackout: loudness collapses to 0.068 at 48.0s, from 0.318 a second earlier (moment 5). The ramp arrives at the top and the track vanishes underneath it. Nothing else to do here.

Moment 6, the climax, intensity 1.00 — the whole band at full strength, 6 families at once. A stab under a full drive bed is invisible, so the climax needs something sharper than the bed. One short burst, not a rave: this is a bhajan.
Loudness 0.153 against 0.316 and 0.230 on either side — a genuine momentary drop in the middle of a 33-second section. A beat of silence in the light where there is one in the track.

Measured hand-off: lead-vocal leads 65.5-67.0s, then back-vocal takes over 67.5-73.5s. The leader hands to the congregation, saffron to rose, one half of the room to the other. trade is the only effect that is both full-rig and genuinely varied.

Moment 7 — lead-vocal re-enters at 72.25s while back-vocal is still on top (0.76 against 0.41). The leader's colour, on two lamps, one beat: he is heard before the room follows him. The trade two bars later is the room following.
The answer. back-vocal falls away after 73.5s and lead-vocal returns 74.0-79.0s, so the colours reverse and the light hands back. Two hand-offs where the music has two, not a trade every bar.

Loudness 0.137 at 80.0s, the second of the chorus's two breathers, and it runs straight into the section 3 arrival. With the drive state not starting until bar 39 this leaves about 1.5s of black — the biggest set-up in the show after the bar 15 hole.
The only thing that reads against a room already at full drive is a beat of nothing first. This is the set-up, not the event.

THE PEAK, moment 9, intensity 1.00. The recording's loudest 0.5s sample is the 92.5-93.0 window and this downbeat sits at 92.76s inside it. The largest gesture in the show, and with the hinge the only other place white goes to full.
Bar 51 is woodwind, harmonica and flute — the one melodic lead in section 4. beam moves only the head, so the pars hold their plateau untouched and the room still changes across eight loud bars.

Spent once, on the last bar of the last chorus, before the outro empties everything. Colour is the right currency for a devotional climax and this is the only place in the show that gets the full wheel.
Moment 11. Drum onsets measure ZERO across 109.8-111.8s and loudness falls 0.356 to 0.054 — the track strips back, so the room does, settling rather than cutting.

The one honest isolate in the song: across 110.8-113.8s only vocal (0.182) and lead-vocal (0.179) are above the floor, every other lane at 0.00-0.05. One lamp, everything else at zero, for a lone voice.

113.0s is the quietest instant in the song, loudness 0.022. The blackout starts later than the isolate so it wins the fixture and takes even that last lamp. Releases at 113.76 as the music returns at 113.5.
Moment 13, intensity 1.00 — lead-vocal, tambourine and vocal all drop out. Loudness sags 0.147 to 0.122 through 115-117s. Four beats only, so it releases exactly as the strings come back at 117.5.

Moment 14, intensity 1.00, register_shift — and the harmony turns to D major at 120.00s in the same breath. The music went up and stayed up, so the light goes up and stays up. The only tier-one gesture here that does not return.
Moment 15, intensity 1.00 — lead-vocal and vocal enter for the last phrase. A swell's envelope is near zero at its own anchor, so the moment needs an instant of its own before the bloom.
Crests at about 125.5s, which is where the outro is fullest: bowed_strings, cello, acoustic-guitar and dobro all at 1.00 and the voice at 0.91. The last bloom of the show, in the major.
Moment 16 — the beat drops away. It starts later than the swell so it cuts through it, and then the swell's tail and the ember drone carry the voice down into the dark.

The invocation. The first struck onset of the song is at 1.81s and loudness crests at 2.0s; this blooms out of the opening black with the lead voice and cello. It is also what stops the opening drone being eight dead seconds — measured at 8.0s of unchanged rig before this was added.
Struck onsets at 6.92 and 7.22s sit either side of this downbeat. A single lamp, which is all bar 3 deserves at 25% loud with one hit - and it is the second thing keeping the opening from parking.
Moment 0. Bar 4 is the first real drum activity in the song — 7 hits, percussion and congas — after bars 1-3 at 1-5. Small, because the moment is intensity 0.235.
Moment 1, intensity 1.00 — synth and back-vocal enter. The responders' first appearance in the song, so it is their colour, and rose does not appear again until the chorus.
The entrance blooms rather than hits — the stab gives the moment its instant, this gives it its shape. Starts a beat later so it cannot cancel the stab.
Moment 2: the tempo really does move, 89.341 to 118.770 bpm at 17.27s, and 1.33 is that exact ratio. Four beats only — gear lifts the whole rig six times a beat and a long one would read as a fault.
Moment 3, intensity 0.93. Inner pair because the last stab took the outer — the extent moves even when the gesture repeats.

The moment is labelled a spotlight but the measurement disagrees: at 21.5-22.5s the texture is at its fullest of the whole intro (14-17 lanes, violin/viola/french-horn/tuba peaking) and lead-vocal does not take the top lane until 23.0s. So it is a bloom that the voice comes out of, not a drop behind one — the swell crests at 23.2s, on the voice.

Bar 13 is the loudest of the three empty bars (55%, a held vocal and synth over 0 drum hits). It is also what stops four bars of drone being four dead seconds — a step is the only thing that breaks a park.
